architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift relative to a matched E2 reactive-core reference without an unacceptable shift in calibrated viscosity level, temperature response, or processability.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Before physical adjudication, predeclare the replicate count, paired or blocked uncertainty estimator, minimum practically meaningful SI reduction, and acceptable viscosity and temperature-response bounds. Accept only if at least two independent S1C41 realizations show lower SI(15-60 min) and SI(15-90 min) than their matched co-prepared E2 controls, with both reductions exceeding the predeclared uncertainty and practical-effect threshold, after candidate-specific 120 C anchoring and validated state calibration where applicable.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail or defer adjudication if either required hold interval is missing, the reduction is not reproducible across at least two independent realizations, the effect does not exceed the predeclared uncertainty and practical threshold, candidate-specific calibration is not validated, modifier functionality or NCO:OH is unresolved, or stability improvement is accompanied by an unacceptable viscosity level, temperature-response shift, or processability change.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Replicate temperature sweeps from 80-130 C with an in-range 120 C anchor; thermal hold at 120 C with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 min; matched co-prepared E2 controls.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The established failure mode is thermal-hold viscosity increase at 120 C, not merely an unfavorable static viscosity. Local experiments show formulation-dependent drift, with E1 substantially more stable than E5, while E2 exhibits large realization/process-state spread. The state-aware rheology analysis supports separating static viscosity, temperature response, and temporal hold stability, and supports one-point calibration within the audited local chemistry; transfer to the modified chemistry remains a testable uncertainty. The selected S1C41 preserves the E2 reactive-core proportions and covers both independently supported intervention axes, using 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor-tackifier-like modifier. The modifier family and broad loading regions come from curated PUR literature/database priors; those priors are analogical or directional and are not treated as predictors of the held-out wet-lab result. The local measurements determine the failure endpoint, E2 comparison basis, state-calibration requirement, and repeatability controls. The conservative design constraints are matched co-prepared E2 controls, verified modifier functionality with recalculated NCO:OH, candidate-specific state anchors, replicate holds, complete process-history records, and predeclared usability and uncertainty rules. S1C40 is rejected as primary because its 2.5% tackifier level is below the supplied evidence-bounded region, while S1C35 has weaker loading support and may be too small relative to E2 variability. The Skeptic's concerns are resolved by reranking to S1C41, requiring stoichiometric verification, candidate-specific calibration validation, paired controls, and operational uncertainty criteria. The Robustness Adjudicator's objection to removing a supported secondary modifier is also resolved: single-axis candidates remain controls for causal isolation, but the declared intent is performance mitigation, for which complete supported-axis coverage is required. This decision identifies an evidence-supported formulation region and experiment, not an exact-property prediction or molecular mechanism.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: This is the required canonical bridge from the upstream rheological analysis. It will determine whether state calibration is necessary, how the temperature-response coordinate should be used, and whether the next experiment should emphasize thermal response, state realization, or hold stability.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective is established, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 reactive-core anchor, independently supported acrylic and tackifier axes, and claim boundary before comparing candidate formulations.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Use source-level chemistry evidence only to bound plausible intervention regions and distinguish directly commensurate numeric anchors from directional or noncommensurate evidence. Do not use it to declare an optimum.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold SI(15 to 60 min) at 120 C
Thermal-hold SI(15 to 90 min) at 120 C
Absolute viscosity level at a predeclared anchor temperature within 80-130 C
Temperature-response slope or equivalent state-aware temperature-sensitivity coordinate within measured support
Need for and consistency after one-point state calibration
Stoichiometric feasibility and reactive-core preservation relative to E2
Distance from directly commensurate external acrylic or tackifier anchors
Whether any apparent stability benefit is accompanied by unacceptable viscosity or processability change
counterfactual_checks: Would the apparent improvement remain if viscosity were compared after state calibration rather than at nominally matched conditions?
Would the conclusion change if the candidate were compared against E1 and E5 using the same 120 C hold schedule and SI calculation?
Could the observed benefit be explained by realization or process history alone, given the E2 run spread?
Does the candidate improve thermal-hold SI without merely shifting the formulation to an unsupported or impractical viscosity range?
Would an E2-only reactive-core control distinguish modifier-axis benefit from process-state variation?
If both acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes are changed, are their loadings independently bounded by the supplied evidence and lattice?
Would the ranking change when thermal response, hold stability, repeatability, and feasibility are evaluated jointly rather than by nominal viscosity alone?
Is any proposed mechanistic interpretation supported by measurements beyond rheology, or should it remain explicitly provisional?
planner.decision_goal: Select one evidence-bounded candidate experiment that mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift while preserving usable viscosity and distinguishing material response from realization/process-state effects.
design_implications: Use thermal-hold SI over the measured 15-90 min window at 120 C as the primary mitigation endpoint.
Evaluate viscosity level and temperature response only within the measured 80-130 C support unless additional support is obtained.
Include process-history, preparation-state, and repeatability checks so a favorable nominal viscosity is not mistaken for a robust material response.
Prefer a candidate region bounded by the supplied evidence-supported modifier ranges; do not convert literature percentages into an exact total-formulation optimum.

A multi-component acrylic-like plus minor tackifier-like intervention is admissible for performance mitigation because both axes have independent external support, provided the candidate remains within the predefined lattice and stoichiometric/process constraints.
Preserve the original E2 reactive-core anchor as the comparison basis and avoid changing unsupported components simultaneously beyond the bounded modifier axes.
Use the state-shift result to determine whether candidate comparison requires one-point state calibration before interpreting viscosity or hold differences.
Do not infer a molecular mechanism from rheology alone; treat modifier functionality and chemistry as hypotheses requiring candidate-level measurement.
material_regularities_to_use: All measured temperature sweeps decrease monotonically from 80 to 130 C and are well described by formulation-specific Andrade-type trends, so temperature response is distinct from time-dependent hold drift.

E2 shows substantial nominal repeat/run spread across the measured temperature range, with sample CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and maximum-to-minimum ratios approximately 2.8-3.6; realization or process state is therefore material to interpretation.
The upstream state-aware analysis must determine whether state shifts collapse onto a master curve and whether one-point state calibration is required before comparing formulations.

The upstream analysis must also establish the local apparent temperature-sensitivity coordinate and the distinct thermal-versus-temporal rheology result; these determine whether the new point needs temperature-response characterization, state calibration, or primarily a thermal hold.
Original thermal-hold behavior differs strongly: E1 has SI(15 to 60 min) approximately 0.095 and SI(15 to 90 min) approximately 0.168, whereas E5 has approximately 0.515 and 0.931.
The local evidence supports thermal-hold stability as an independent design objective rather than optimizing only viscosity at one temperature.

External evidence supports acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifier axes as chemically plausible directions, but the supplied anchors are analogical or directional and do not establish a local optimum or mechanism.
planner.physical_failure_mode: The established failure is thermal-hold viscosity increase at 120 C, with a large contrast between original E1 and E5 hold drift. Nominal viscosity is also confounded by substantial E2 run-to-run spread, so the next experiment must address hold stability without treating a single nominal viscosity value as an intrinsic material property.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep covering the measured 80-130 C range, with a predeclared anchor temperature inside that range
At least one-point state calibration or equivalent state descriptor if the upstream master-curve result shows state dependence
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 C with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 min, preserving the SI definition SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0
Replicate temperature-sweep measurements sufficient to quantify nominal spread, CV, and maximum-to-minimum ratio
Replicate thermal-hold measurements or a documented process-history comparison sufficient to separate hold behavior from realization variability
Recorded formulation identity, modifier loadings, reactive-core composition, stoichiometry, preparation history, preconditioning, and measurement conditions
Viscosity units and raw or traceable trajectory data, with unknown values left unknown rather than imputed
Comparison against the original E2 reactive-core anchor and the original E1/E5 hold-stability references
uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary does not establish whether state calibration is required.
The candidate lies outside the measured 80-130 C temperature support or outside the measured 15-90 min hold window.
A favorable result depends on a single nominal run despite E2-like repeatability spread.
Process history, preconditioning, or realization state is undocumented or differs materially from the reference.
The candidate changes stoichiometry or reactive-core composition beyond the evidence-supported design space.
External evidence is only directional, noncommensurate, or lacks a thermal-hold measurement.
Acrylic or tackifier functionality is treated as a proven mechanism rather than a hypothesis.
Hold data are incomplete, nonmonotonic without explanation, or unavailable at the adjudication times.
The candidate shows improved hold stability but unacceptable viscosity level or temperature response.
The observed difference is smaller than the measured repeatability uncertainty.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The selected full-coverage candidate mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift relative to the matched E2 reactive-core reference without creating an unacceptable viscosity or temperature-response shift.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
